easy.explanation: Jonah prayed to the LORD out of the fish’s belly.
The verse says that Jonah prayed unto the LORD his God.
“Belly” refers to the inside of the fish where Jonah was.
easy.q: What does the word “belly” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: Jonah prayed to the LORD from inside the fish.
medium.q: What did Jonah do while he was inside the fish?

answers: He was searching for a city
medium.explanation: Praying from the fish’s belly shows that Jonah was in a desperate situation.
medium.q: What does Jonah’s prayer show about his situation?

medium.explanation: The phrase “out of the fish’s belly” identifies Jonah’s location.
medium.q: Which phrase identifies the fish as the place from which Jonah prayed?

answers: He turned to God even in extreme danger
He did not know where he was
He wanted to remain inside the fish
challenge.explanation: Jonah’s prayer shows that he turned to God even while facing extreme danger.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Jonah praying from inside the fish?

answers: It presents Jonah’s prayer as a personal appeal to God
It says Jonah prayed to the fish
It shows that Jonah had forgotten God
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes Jonah’s personal relationship with and appeal to the LORD.
challenge.q: How does the phrase “the LORD his God” shape the meaning of the passage?

answers: Jonah is in danger and responds by praying
Jonah reaches land and begins preaching
Jonah escapes the sea without speaking
challenge.explanation: The passage focuses on Jonah’s dangerous location and his prayer to God.
challenge.q: What is the main movement in these verses?

paragraphs.title: The Cry to the Lord and Hope in Prayer

easy.explanation: Jonah says, “I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the LORD.”
easy.q: To whom did Jonah cry from his affliction?

easy.explanation: Jonah describes the deep, the seas, the floods, the billows, and the waves around him.
easy.q: What surrounded Jonah according to his prayer?

easy.explanation: Jonah said, “yet I will look again toward thy holy temple.”
easy.q: What did Jonah say he would look toward?

answers: Because of his journey to land
medium.explanation: The phrase explains that Jonah cried to the LORD because he was suffering.
medium.q: What does “by reason of mine affliction” mean?

medium.explanation: “The deep” refers to the depths of the sea into which Jonah had been cast.
medium.q: What is the best meaning of “the deep” in this passage?

answers: He says he will look again toward God’s holy temple
He says he will stop praying
He says the waves have disappeared
medium.explanation: Although Jonah feels cast out of God’s sight, he still hopes to look toward the holy temple.
medium.q: How does Jonah express hope despite feeling cast out?

answers: He feels far from God, yet still hopes to turn toward Him
He fears the ship but wants to return to it
He dislikes the sea but wants to remain in it
challenge.explanation: Jonah feels separated from God but continues to express hope and faith.
challenge.q: What is the central tension in Jonah’s words?

answers: They portray Jonah’s situation as dangerous and overwhelming
They prove that Jonah was on dry land
They show that Jonah was celebrating
challenge.explanation: The water imagery emphasizes the danger and distress from which Jonah cries out.
challenge.q: How do the descriptions of floods, billows, and waves strengthen the prayer?

answers: It introduces hope in contrast with Jonah’s despair
It shows that Jonah has stopped praying
It explains that the sea has become calm
challenge.explanation: “Yet” contrasts Jonah’s feeling of rejection with his continuing hope toward God.
challenge.q: What does the word “yet” contribute to the statement “yet I will look again”?

paragraphs.title: Descent into the Sea and Rescue from Destruction

easy.explanation: Jonah says, “the weeds were wrapped about my head.”
easy.q: What was wrapped around Jonah’s head?

answers: To the bottoms of the mountains
To the top of a hill
easy.explanation: Jonah says, “I went down to the bottoms of the mountains.”

easy.q: Whom did Jonah remember when his soul fainted?

answers: A feeling of being shut in
medium.explanation: The image of bars describes Jonah’s sense of confinement.
medium.q: What does the phrase “the earth with her bars was about me” describe?

medium.explanation: The weeds are sea plants surrounding Jonah in the water.
medium.q: What are “the weeds” in this context?

answers: His prayer came into God’s holy temple
medium.explanation: Jonah says that when he remembered the LORD, his prayer came into the holy temple.
medium.q: What happened when Jonah remembered the LORD?

answers: Jonah is trapped and near destruction, yet his prayer reaches God
Jonah is safe on land, yet he describes a calm sea
Jonah is joyful in the temple, yet he fears the city
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts Jonah’s confinement and danger with the access represented by his prayer.
challenge.q: What contrast appears in these verses?

answers: He moves from the waters to the depths and feels enclosed by the earth
He moves from the shore to a ship and then to a mountain
He moves from the temple into the fish and then onto land
challenge.explanation: Jonah describes sinking into the deep, reaching the mountains’ bottoms, and being enclosed by the earth.
challenge.q: How does Jonah’s description of descending develop?

answers: The LORD rescued Jonah from death and destruction
Jonah chose to sink deeper into the sea
The fish swallowed the entire sea
challenge.explanation: The statement credits the LORD with bringing Jonah’s life up from corruption, or destruction.
challenge.q: What does “yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption” imply?

paragraphs.title: Faithfulness to the Lord and Thanksgiving for Salvation

easy.explanation: Jonah says that those who observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy.
easy.q: What do people who observe lying vanities forsake?

easy.explanation: Jonah says, “I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving.”
easy.q: What did Jonah promise to offer with the voice of thanksgiving?

easy.explanation: Jonah declares, “Salvation is of the LORD.”
easy.q: Who is the source of salvation according to Jonah?

medium.explanation: Jonah says, “I will pay that that I have vowed.”
medium.q: What did Jonah promise to do with what he had vowed?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to empty, worthless, or deceptive objects of trust.
medium.q: What does “lying vanities” most nearly mean?

answers: Jonah gives thanks and acknowledges that salvation comes from the LORD
Jonah thanks the fish and credits it with salvation
medium.explanation: Jonah promises thanksgiving and concludes that salvation belongs to the LORD.
medium.q: How are thanksgiving and salvation connected in Jonah’s words?

answers: Jonah turns to the LORD instead of trusting worthless things
Jonah compares two kinds of fish
Jonah says that every prayer is worthless
challenge.explanation: Jonah contrasts faithfulness to the LORD with reliance on empty or deceptive things.
challenge.q: What contrast is made between Jonah and those who observe lying vanities?

answers: Thanksgiving, fulfillment of a vow, and recognition that salvation is of the LORD
Flight, forgetfulness, and refusal to give thanks
Building an altar, reaching land, and falling asleep
challenge.explanation: Jonah promises thanksgiving, vows to pay what he vowed, and declares that salvation is of the LORD.
challenge.q: Which sequence of ideas appears in Jonah’s statement?

answers: He attributes deliverance to the LORD
He attributes deliverance to the fish
challenge.explanation: Jonah explicitly says that salvation comes from the LORD.
challenge.q: What does “Salvation is of the LORD” reveal about Jonah’s understanding?

paragraphs.title: The Fish Brings Jonah onto Dry Land

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the LORD spake unto the fish.”
easy.q: To whom did the LORD speak?

easy.explanation: The fish vomited Jonah out after receiving the LORD’s command.
easy.q: What did the fish do after the LORD spoke?

easy.explanation: The fish brought Jonah upon the dry land.

answers: Land that is not covered by water
medium.explanation: Dry land is the solid ground where Jonah was placed.
medium.q: What does “dry land” mean in this verse?

medium.explanation: The fish released Jonah after the LORD spoke to it.
medium.q: What caused the fish to release Jonah?

answers: The fish brings him onto dry land
The fish leaves him in the deep
Jonah chooses to return to the fish
medium.explanation: The verse ends with Jonah being brought safely onto dry land.
medium.q: How does the verse conclude Jonah’s time inside the fish?

answers: As an instrument under the LORD’s command
As a creature Jonah chose to enter
challenge.explanation: The fish first preserves Jonah and later releases him in response to the LORD’s command.
challenge.q: How is the fish presented in the larger account?

answers: The fish’s obedience brings about Jonah’s deliverance to dry land
The fish proves that it, rather than the LORD, is the source of salvation
The fish cancels the meaning of Jonah’s prayer
challenge.explanation: Because the fish acts at the LORD’s command, Jonah’s rescue demonstrates that salvation is of the LORD.
challenge.q: How does this verse connect with Jonah’s declaration that salvation is of the LORD?

answers: He moves from confinement inside the fish to safety on dry land
He moves from dry land into the sea
He moves from prayer into deeper confinement
challenge.explanation: Jonah changes from being inside the fish to being placed upon dry land.
challenge.q: What change in Jonah’s condition is described?
